findings.desc: Closeout receipt replay does not prove the current write was canonical. latestValidCloseoutReceipt accepts any historical receipt whose artifactDigest matches current bytes and whose headHash is merely an ancestor; it does not bind the receipt to the commit/change under review or require the receipt to be newly minted with that artifact change. Reverting an artifact manually to previously receipted bytes therefore reuses the old canonical writer claim and passes retention. More generally receiptHash is recomputable from a public salt, so a manual writer can self-assert a canonical writerCommand. This violates CHK-004/CHK-005 manual, replayed, and stale-provenance fail-closed guarantees.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 812a711565: v2 per-artifact integrity chain requires the latest receipt, intact sequence/previous hash, receipt introduction commit equal to latest artifact-changing commit, and receipt pre-write head equal to that commit parent. Exact A to B to manual A replay, copy, and reorder regressions pass. npm test and closeout smoke pass.

findings.desc: The delivery-context runtime validator accepts semantically invalid payloads that CHK-003 says must fail closed. validatePersistedDeliveryContextPack leaves candidateRouting and validation completely unchecked, does not exact-key or type-check claims, accepts non-string entries in diff.changedFiles/testFiles/evidenceCommands, and does not validate deliveryCheck.ref. A structurally plausible pack such as changedFiles:[42] with arbitrary candidateRouting/validation and extra claims fields is treated as trusted, while the smoke only tests authorityDone=true. Tighten the persisted schema to the producer contract and add adversarial cases.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 812a711565: delivery context now exact-validates claims, string arrays, candidate routing, validation evidence, review round, delivery ref, and waiver nested shapes. Adversarial malformed nested payload regressions pass.

findings.desc: Receipt replay defeats the claimed manual/stale-write rejection. latestValidCloseoutReceipt filters all historical receipts for the path and returns any matching valid record, so after canonical A then canonical B, a manual revert of the artifact to A is accepted under the old receipt even though the latest write was not canonical. Reproduced against dist: receipts [A@2026-01-01,B@2026-01-02] plus current summary.json=A returned acceptedTimestamp=2026-01-01. Bind receipts to the actual write/commit and reject superseded/replayed receipts (including copied/reordered receipt-ledger entries).
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 812a711565. Only the final intact receipt-chain entry can qualify, and its introduction commit must equal the latest artifact-changing commit with pre-write HEAD as parent. A-to-B-to-manual-A replay, copy, and reorder regressions pass.

findings.desc: The 15-intent evidence overstates CLI/integration coverage. CHK-004 is type=cli and requires canonical parent_ledger_rollup_set output, but closeout-trust-smoke never invokes that handler/CLI; it calls store.writeProofStoryParentLedgerRollup plus autoCommitStoryMetadata directly. Likewise none of the newly wired validate, done_required_validate, delivery_check_set/waiver, evaluate_save, summary_set, delivery_context_pack, or live_smoke_transcript handler paths are executed. The smoke can stay green if a handler omits or passes the wrong closeoutArtifactPaths. Add at least one real CLI/handler regression for parent_ledger_rollup_set and table-driven integration coverage for every registered canonical writer path; wire this high-risk smoke into routine test discovery/evidence.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 812a711565. The closeout smoke executes all supported canonical writer-path pairs through real handlers, including parent rollup and legacy test writers, and routine npm test includes test:closeout-trust. Full npm test exits 0.

findings.desc: Trusted artifact runtime schemas accept missing required timestamps and semantically invalid delivery-context fields. Repro after the story build: calling validateTrustedMilestoneLedger with createdAt removed, validateTrustedSlicePlan with updatedAt removed, and validateTrustedParentLedgerRollup with createdAt removed all return successfully; validatePersistedDeliveryContextPack also accepts changedFiles:[42], testFiles:[42], evidenceCommands:[{}], and deliveryCheck.ref as a string. This contradicts CHK-003 edge/adversarial and means malformed persisted payloads can cross the new trust boundary. Require/validate createdAt+updatedAt (including ISO shape), validate optional typed fields/semantic relationships, require string arrays for delivery paths/commands, validate ref null/object and exact claims shape, and add negative regressions.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 812a711565. Ledger, plan, and rollup require ISO createdAt and updatedAt plus strict nested fields; delivery pack nested schema is exact. Missing timestamp and malformed payload regressions pass.

findings.desc: The closed writer-provenance table names writers that cannot produce the receipts required by the real retention gate. test-evidence.json lists test_add/test_story, but those handlers write the artifact without autoCommitStoryMetadata(closeoutArtifactPaths), so their declared canonical output is always rejected as missing/stale receipt. More critically, evidence/transcript-diff.md is assigned to live_smoke_transcript, but that command only writes evidence/live-smoke-transcript.json; the TEST lifecycle hint still instructs users to hand-write transcript-diff.md. Following that normal closeout instruction therefore invalidates review retention, and the verifier only checks that writer command names exist, not that they attest the listed path. Align the closed policy with real writer choke points (or add explicit CLI writers/receipts), preserve intentional legacy compatibility, and add an end-to-end regression for every declared path/writer pair.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 812a711565. test_add and test_story now attest test evidence; test_story commits after final metadata write; phantom transcript-diff policy is removed; TEST UX directs canonical live smoke JSON with an explicit capture command. Every policy writer pair runs in smoke.

findings.desc: The v2 chain closes historical replay/copy/reorder, but still does not prove the current write came from a canonical handler. Every receipt field and integrityHash is publicly computable. Reproduced in a fresh git repo without calling summary_set or autoCommitStoryMetadata: manually write summary.json plus a sequence=1 receipt claiming writerCommand=summary_set, set headHash/materialHash/storyFilesHash to the parent, commit both together, and latestValidCloseoutReceipt accepts it (accepted=true, writer=summary_set). This violates CHK-001 canonical writer provenance and CHK-004 adversarial manual/wrong-writer rejection. Add an authority boundary the manual writer cannot mint (or narrow the claim/threat model and intents); include this exact counterfeit-current-receipt negative in the smoke.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 065b7dde13: closeout receipts are now signed by a per-story/per-review-round Ed25519 key whose public identity is bound into the exact ReviewRun; manual co-commit forgery, wrong-key signing, signer rotation replay, and old-key replay are rejected by regression coverage.

findings.desc: F-001 was only partially resolved: the v2 chain prevents historical receipt replay, but it still does not distinguish a canonical CLI write from a hand-crafted co-commit. Repro against current dist created summary.json manually, built a v2 receipt with writerCommand=summary_set using the exported deterministic builder, committed artifact+receipt together with an arbitrary manual commit, and latestValidCloseoutReceipt returned ACCEPTED forged writer=summary_set. The causal checks all pass because artifactCommit equals receipt introductionCommit and receipt.headHash is its parent. Reclassifying the receipt as non-signed is honest, but CHK-001 canonical writer provenance and CHK-004/CHK-005 manual-write fail-closed guarantees still require a mechanically trusted writer fact. Bind provenance to an existing non-forgeable/controlled command event or signed CLI artifact, or narrow the acceptance claim; add this exact forged co-commit regression.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 065b7dde13: the causal receipt no longer trusts a self-reported public key; verification is anchored to the signer identity embedded in the exact signed ReviewRun and rejects independently minted co-commit receipts.

findings.desc: Canonical closeout receipt/auto-commit is broken for a valid wrapper-root layout where metadataRoot differs from gitRoot and storyDir is configured inside gitRoot (for example gitRoot=repo, storyDir=repo/.lattice/story/actives). autoCommitStoryMetadata resolves gitCwd to <wrapper>/repo but constructs storyRel directly from the metadata-root-relative config and probes <gitCwd>/repo/.lattice/...; the actual story is <gitCwd>/.lattice/.... In a real temp Git reproduction evaluateStoryDirInsideGitRoot returned ok:true with rel=.lattice/story/actives/B-wrap, while autoCommitStoryMetadata returned an empty hint and git status retained ?? .lattice/. Thus canonical closeout writers silently produce neither commit nor receipt and later retention/clean-tree gates fail. Derive the staged/provenance path by relativizing the canonical StoryStore storyDirPath against resolved gitCwd (and fail closed if outside), and add wrapper-root receipt coverage.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 065b7dde13: wrapper-root story-relative paths now use canonical realpath containment relative to the git root, preventing doubled prefixes; the real wrapper-root autoCommit and receipt regression passes.

findings.desc: The Ed25519 repair still does not establish the claimed exact ReviewRun-bound canonical writer provenance. The private key is stored as plaintext mode-0600 under project-accessible .lattice/runtime and is returned by the exported loadReviewRoundReceiptSigner/loadOrCreateReviewRoundReceiptSigner API, so the same local actor that can hand-write story metadata can read the trusted key and sign a forged co-commit. Repro against current dist: load the round signer, manually write summary.json, build a receipt claiming writerCommand=summary_set, sign it with signer.privateKey, append and commit both; latestValidCloseoutReceipt returns `ACCEPTED exact-key manual forge`. The current smoke tests only an attacker-generated wrong key. Also the signer path hashes only reviewRound, and repeated loadOrCreate calls in one round return the same key (`sameRoundKeyReused true`), so it is round-scoped rather than exact-ReviewRun scoped as claimed. Keep the signing capability outside the manual writer threat domain and bind/authorize it per exact reviewRunId (or narrow the contract honestly); add correct-key exfiltration and same-round distinct-run regressions.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by c7fc14674c and f10e43b8ee: removed persistent review-round signer authority and narrowed local receipts to audit-only causal telemetry. latestValidCloseoutReceipt now deliberately rejects all same-UID local receipts; the real consumer proves an exact coherent manual forge remains inadmissible and a fresh post-closeout review succeeds.

findings.desc: Wrapper-root metadata retention still uses the metadata-root-relative configured storyDir as though it were git-root-relative. In evaluateReviewRunMetadataRetention, projectRoot is the resolved git root and changedFilesBetween returns .lattice/story/actives/B-wrap/..., but storyPrefix is built from store.storyDirRel() as repo/.lattice/story/actives/B-wrap/. The filter therefore sees no changed story artifacts. A real split-root fixture with gitRoot=repo and storyDir=repo/.lattice/story/actives committed unknown-manual.json after the review snapshot; git diff reported .lattice/story/actives/B-wrap/unknown-manual.json while evaluateReviewRunMetadataRetention returned {ok:true,reasons:[]}. Rebase the canonical StoryStore story directory relative to projectRoot exactly as autoCommit now does, reject outside paths, and cover unknown/manual plus canonical receipt cases through the real retention consumer in wrapper-root mode.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by c7fc14674c: metadata-only retention now derives story paths canonically relative to gitRoot under wrapper-root configurations. The real wrapper fixture commits unknown-manual.json and the retention consumer rejects it with the named path; scope/process contracts pass.

findings.desc: The new Ed25519 key does not authenticate that a write came from a canonical command against the stated same-workspace manual-writer adversary. The private key is a predictable local runtime file readable by the same OS user that can hand-edit story metadata, and loadReviewRoundReceiptSigner plus signCloseoutWriteReceipt are directly usable by that process. In a real wrapper fixture I loaded the exact review-round private key, manually wrote summary.json, built a receipt claiming writerCommand=summary_set with the current HEAD/hashes, appended it, and committed both; latestValidCloseoutReceipt accepted it. The regression only uses an independently generated attacker key, so it misses this capability-reuse attack. Mode 0600 separates OS users but cannot distinguish the canonical CLI from manual code running as the project user (and load does not reject a key file whose mode has become permissive). Either use a signer capability isolated from arbitrary project-user reads, or narrow the claim/threat model; add a same-key manual co-commit regression.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by c7fc14674c and f10e43b8ee: mode-0600 same-UID key storage was removed from the authority model and runtime registry. Local receipts are explicitly audit-only; exact same-UID artifact plus coherent receipt forgery is accepted only as causal telemetry and rejected by gate-authoritative lookup, requiring fresh review.

findings.desc: The implementation correctly makes local causal receipts audit-only, but the process-fact registry still falsely classifies closeout-write-receipts.jsonl as gate evidence. The entry retains semantics=[artifact,schema-contract,freshness-policy,gate-evidence] and consumerGate=REVIEW evidence metadata-only retention gate, while REVIEW_RETENTION_PROTOCOL_METADATA_PATHS explicitly ignores the receipt file, latestValidCloseoutReceipt returns null without reading it, and latestCausallyValidCloseoutReceipt has no production consumer. This contradicts the registry rationale (not authority/not closeout evidence) and the project rule that gate-consumed facts must match actual mechanical consumers. Reclassify the artifact as audit/telemetry with no gate-evidence semantic or claimed consumer; keep the fail-closed authoritative boundary as the L4 runtime gate fact.

Revised receipt semantics are honest at the helper boundary, but the promised fresh-review requirement is not mechanically enforced on the actual TEST→DONE path. evaluateReviewRunMetadataRetention/collectReviewerEvidenceState reject a pre-closeout review after closeout metadata changes, yet canFinishGuard never consumes either function; reviewer evidence is checked only on REVIEW→TEST. Therefore a TEST-phase closeout writer can change summary/test/delivery metadata and still reach DONE through the remaining DONE gates without a fresh reviewer pass. The smoke test only constructs a synthetic fresh RR-002 and calls the helper directly while the story is in TEST, so it does not prove lifecycle enforcement. Add TEST/DONE gate consumption plus an end-to-end transition regression, while accounting for legitimate REVIEW→TEST phase/index mutations so the new gate does not self-invalidate every pass.
